title: Camping in India: Best Places and How to Camp Well
seoTitle: Camping in India: Best Places & How to Camp Well | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: The best places for camping in India, from Rishikesh riverside camps and Jaisalmer desert camps to Pangong, Chandratal, Chopta and Pawna Lake, plus rules and tips.
description: A guide to camping in India: riverside camps near Rishikesh, desert camps at Sam and Khuri, the Rann Utsav tent city, high-altitude camps at Pangong and Chandratal, meadow camps at Chopta and Sonamarg, lakeside camping at Pawna and Bhandardara, and the rules and etiquette to follow.
dek: Camping in India ranges from comfortable tent resorts in the desert to wild camps on Himalayan treks. Here is where to go and how to camp responsibly.

hero.alt: Nomad camp tents in a high valley at Rajung Karu, Ladakh
hero.caption: Rajung Karu, Ladakh

intro: Most camping in India is not wild camping but staying in fixed tent camps: rows of Swiss-style tents with beds, attached bathrooms and a dining tent, set up by a river, lake, dune or meadow. They are an easy way to spend a night outdoors with a bonfire and stars, and they suit families and first-timers.

True wild camping happens mostly on treks, where operators pitch dome tents at campsites along the route. In between are simple lakeside and forest camps near the big cities. This guide covers the best places for each and the rules that apply, since camping has been restricted in some sensitive areas.
quickAnswer: The best places for camping in India include riverside camps near Rishikesh, desert camps at Sam and Khuri near Jaisalmer, the Rann Utsav tent city in Kutch, lakeside camps at Pangong Tso and near Chandratal, meadow camps at Chopta, Sonamarg and Kasol, and lakeside camping at Pawna Lake and Bhandardara in Maharashtra. Choose licensed camps, check local rules and carry warm layers for mountain nights.
takeaways: Most camps in India are fixed tent camps with beds and bathrooms; wild camping is mostly on treks.
Desert camps near Jaisalmer and the Rann Utsav in Kutch are winter experiences.
High camps at Pangong and Chandratal are summer only, and very cold at night.
Camping on river beaches, alpine meadows and near some lakes has been restricted by courts and authorities.
Leave no trace: carry out rubbish, avoid plastic and keep noise down.

sections.heading: Best places for camping in India

items.name: Rishikesh, Uttarakhand
body: Camps in the forest and on land above the Ganga between Shivpuri and Kaudiyala combine a night outdoors with river rafting, a bonfire and short walks. Choose licensed camps; camping on the river beaches themselves has been restricted.

items.name: Sam and Khuri, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
body: Tent camps near the dunes at Sam and quieter Khuri, about 40 km from Jaisalmer, offer camel rides, folk music and dinners under desert skies. Some camps are sold as luxury tents, others are simple.

image.alt: Camel safari on the Sam sand dunes near Jaisalmer
image.caption: Sam dunes, Jaisalmer

items.name: Rann Utsav tent city, Kutch, Gujarat
body: During the Rann Utsav, a tent city is set up at Dhordo on the edge of the white salt desert, with cultural programmes and full-moon nights on the Rann.

items.name: Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri, Ladakh
body: Tent camps along the shores of Pangong at villages such as Spangmik, and near Tso Moriri at Korzok, give sunrise on high-altitude lakes. Nights are freezing even in summer, and the altitude is over 4,200 metres, so acclimatise in Leh first.

image.alt: Tent camps on the shore of Pangong Tso
image.caption: Pangong Tso

items.name: Chandratal, Himachal Pradesh
body: Camps near the crescent-shaped lake on the Spiti side of Kunzum Pass have been moved back from the shore to protect it; you walk the last stretch. Open only when the road over Kunzum is open.

items.name: Chopta, Uttarakhand
body: Tents on the edge of the Chopta meadows are the base for the Tungnath and Chandrashila walk, with views of the Chaukhamba massif.

facts.Season: Most of the year; snow in winter

image.alt: Tents on the meadow at Chopta with Himalayan peaks behind
image.caption: Chopta

items.name: Parvati Valley and Kasol, Himachal Pradesh
body: Riverside and forest camps around Kasol and on the Kheerganga trek are popular with young travellers. Check that camps are licensed and avoid unregulated sites.

facts.Season: April to June, September to November

items.name: Pawna Lake and Bhandardara, Maharashtra
body: Lakeside camps near Lonavala at Pawna, and at Bhandardara near Igatpuri, are easy overnight trips from Mumbai and Pune. Bhandardara is known for fireflies before the monsoon.

items.name: Shnongpdeng, Meghalaya
body: Riverside camping on the clear Umngot river near Dawki, with kayaking, snorkelling in the clear water and cliff jumping nearby.

rows: Rishikesh, Jaisalmer, Rann of Kutch, Pangong
Large furnished tents, sometimes with heating
Dome tents, sleeping bags, kitchen tent

sections.heading: Rules and restrictions
paras: Camping rules in India are set by state governments, forest departments and courts, and they change. Camping on the Ganga's river beaches near Rishikesh has been restricted; overnight camping in some high-altitude meadows (bugyals) in Uttarakhand has been limited by court orders; and camps near lakes such as Chandratal and Pangong have been moved back from the shore.

Inside national parks and wildlife sanctuaries, camping is allowed only at designated sites with permits. Wild camping on private or village land needs permission. When in doubt, stay at a licensed camp.

sections.heading: Camping tips
list: Check what is included: meals, bathrooms, blankets or sleeping bags, and activities.
In the mountains, nights can be near or below freezing even in summer; carry warm layers and a cap.
Carry a headlamp or torch; camps are dark away from the dining area.
Keep food sealed and inside tents to avoid attracting animals.
Keep music low; sound carries far in the outdoors.
Carry all rubbish back with you, including cigarette butts and wrappers.

safety: Book licensed camps with proper toilets, lighting and emergency plans.
Avoid camping on riverbeds and near streams in the monsoon; water levels can rise suddenly.
Check wildlife advice in forest areas and follow the camp's rules after dark.
At high altitude, acclimatise before sleeping above about 3,500 metres.
Keep bonfires small and in designated spots, and put them out completely.
packing: Warm layers and a cap for the night
A small bag for your rubbish

faqs.q: Where is the best camping in India?
faqs.a: Rishikesh, Jaisalmer, the Rann of Kutch, Pangong Tso, Chandratal, Chopta, Kasol and Pawna Lake are among the most popular places.

faqs.q: Is wild camping allowed in India?
faqs.a: Only in some places. Camping is restricted in many river, meadow and protected areas, and on private land you need permission. Licensed camps are the safest option.

faqs.q: When is the best time for desert camping in Rajasthan?
faqs.a: October to March, when the desert is cool.
Yes. Pawna Lake near Lonavala and Bhandardara are popular lakeside camping spots.

faqs.q: Is camping at Pangong Lake open all year?
faqs.a: No. Camps operate roughly from May to September, when roads are open and nights are cold but bearable.
